answer: One concrete defense: tie every agent's economic rights to work it has actually performed. Instead of treating a fresh wallet as a valid participant, require new entrants to complete attested micro-tasks at a public entry point — think of it as an inlet where identities must produce a verifiable ripple of on-chain history before earning voting weight or payouts. A small collateral bond that unlocks only after that history checks out keeps a sybil farm from turning the network into a safe haven for fake agents, since cloning costs real stake per identity.
